clue.text: Wet bear hid nuts for food

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the three words before it go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: A soaked bear has stashed nuts away as its food supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the hidden food, but it is the anagram signal working on WETBEARHID.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft sliced loaf made from refined flour is a basic foodstuff, so the term names a kind of food.

clue.text: Part of speech that's hummed out loud

indicators.note: out loud means the synonym for hummed is to be heard spoken rather than read on the page

parts.note: a machine that hummed or buzzed can be said to have whirred

explanation.surface: Someone asks which part of speech a tune hummed out loud would count as.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent WHIRRED and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A single unit of language is a component of anything spoken, so it is literally a piece of speech.

clue.text: Press learning to support naughty child

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits below the other one, so the learning goes beneath the child

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
lore is traditional knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: An instruction to push education so as to help a badly behaved youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' is a positional signal that only works in a down entry: LORE ends up under IMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to urge or beg them earnestly, which is to plead with them.

clue.text: Bug lover with awkward set-to looming

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy disorder, so the letters of the set-to looming are jumbled

explanation.surface: An insect enthusiast faces an uncomfortable quarrel that is about to break out.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies insects is fond of bugs, so a playful description of that specialist is a bug lover.

clue.text: Brett, Nick and René all discovered time is backward

indicators.note: discovered means with the cover taken off, so each of the three names loses its outside letters

explanation.surface: Three named people find out that time runs in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all discovered' uncovers each name, leaving its inside letters; 'backward' looks like a reversal signal but it is the definition, meaning shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Backward can mean shy or reluctant to come forward, which matches being reserved and quiet.

clue.text: Number initially applauded on stage

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word applauded

parts.note: to stage a play or show is to mount it

explanation.surface: A musical number is clapped from the start once it is performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' in the surface is a song, but it is the definition as a quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A number in the sense of a quantity or total is a synonym for a sum of something.

clue.text: Annoy leaving parking place

indicators.note: leaving says the parking letter departs from the verb meaning annoy

parts.note: to spite someone is to annoy or hurt them deliberately
P is the standard sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A driver gets irritated on being turned away from a parking spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A location or position where something stands is a place, the plain synonym here.

clue.text: Take off some Chinese tat I'm ironing when upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the run of letters reads from bottom to top
some means only a part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone pressing cheap Chinese trinkets is copied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ETATIMI from Chinese tat I'm ironing, and 'when upset' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off a person is to mimic or parody them, a colloquial synonym for copying.

clue.text: Sour beer found in Eastern Mediterranean

indicators.note: found in says the beer sits inside the letters from Eastern and Mediterranean

parts.note: bitter is a British style of hoppy draught ale

explanation.surface: Someone finds the beer on a holiday in the eastern Med has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER is a hoppy British draught ale; it goes between the E and the M of EMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour as an adjective for a person means resentful and full of grievance, as is someone soured by events.

clue.text: Name European plant in allotment

indicators.note: in places the European and plant letters inside the word for an allotment

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allotment or share
to plant something is to put it in place

explanation.surface: A gardener names a European plant growing in their allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' is the verb meaning put, not a growing thing; an allotment in Britain is a rented garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A good name in the sense of standing or repute is what people think of you.

clue.text: Member's loveless dance

indicators.note: loveless means the zero letter, love in tennis scoring, is removed

parts.note: the limbo is a dance under a lowered bar

explanation.surface: A club member is doing a dance without any affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis, so O is dropped; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a member of the body, an old anatomical sense.

clue.text: Limit short show with clowns, medium and writer

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off the word for the show

parts.note: a circus is a show with clowns and acrobats
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A demand to cut back a show featuring clowns, a psychic and an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' suggests a psychic but here it is just the size letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict something within bounds is to draw a line around it, a formal synonym for limit.

clue.text: Place to sleep in empty room after party

indicators.note: after puts the room letters behind the party word

parts.note: a do is a party or social event

indicators.note: empty means the inside of room is removed, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone needs somewhere to crash in a vacant room after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormitory, shortened, is a shared bedroom in a school or college.

clue.text: Close friend certain East will go for ace

indicators.note: go for means take the place of, so the ace letter replaces the East letter

parts.note: certain means sure or assured
E is the compass abbreviation for East
A is the abbreviation for ace in playing cards

explanation.surface: A bridge player is sure an intimate pal sitting East will lead an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players are North, South, East and West, which is the surface's card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone you trust with secrets is an intimate companion, the person you confide in.

clue.text: Fortune-hunter in favour of area seizing power

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of

indicators.note: seizing means the area word grabs the power letter and holds it inside

parts.note: a sector is an area or zone
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A gold-digger backs a region taking control.
explanation.definitionFit: A miner searching for gold or minerals is literally hunting a fortune.

clue.text: Druidess occasionally left mixture of gin and wine

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of Druidess, starting with the first
mixture of says the three letters of the spirit are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A priestess sometimes left a cocktail of gin and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A white grape variety from Germany and Alsace gives its name to a dry or sweet white wine.

clue.text: Seem confused about church plan

indicators.note: about means the muddled letters go around the church abbreviation
confused means the letters of seem are muddled

explanation.surface: People appear bewildered by a church's plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme and a plan are synonyms for a set arrangement for getting something done.

clue.text: Stirring part of service

parts.note: stirring suggests rousing, and service a church or military one; here it is a tea service and the piece of cutlery that stirs the cups

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' reads as exciting and 'service' as a ceremony, but a tea set comes with small spoons for stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon in a tea set is the item used to stir sugar into each cup.

clue.text: Runners on this small step

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase: the thing that runners are fixed on

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a ledge is a narrow shelf or step

explanation.surface: Athletes are told to take a little step up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' are not athletes but the long strips a sled glides on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled for snow travels on two runners, so it is the vehicle the runners belong to.

clue.text: Tax producer of emissions

definitions.meaning: to tax someone is to wear them out or tire them
the pipe on a car through which fumes leave the engine

explanation.definitionFit: Draining someone's strength and the tailpipe venting engine fumes share one word.

clue.text: Potter's friend mostly solitary and single

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, dropping its final letter

parts.note: a solitary, as a noun, is a recluse or hermit
single means one

explanation.surface: A potter's pal is mostly a loner and unmarried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' is Harry Potter, not a craftsman at a wheel; his friend is Hermione Granger.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermione Granger is Harry Potter's best friend in the J. K. Rowling books.

clue.text: Something blown from retro car in accident

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something is blown out of a vintage car after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' and 'accident' look like reversal and anagram signals but are just the text the letters lie in.
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped wind instrument is played by blowing into it.

clue.text: Shock arrangement?

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair, so the arrangement of a shock is a style for it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as a fright, but it is a mop of hair, as in a shock of red hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A styled arrangement of the hair on a head is a coiffure.

clue.text: See pin has damaged letter

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of the three words before it are broken and put back in another order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look at how a pin has torn a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is not a character of the alphabet but an epistle: St Paul's letter to the church at Ephesus in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Testament epistle written by Paul to the Christians of Ephesus is a book in the form of a letter.

clue.text: Flatter fizzy drinks for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means the word is to be heard by listeners, so its sound counts

parts.note: Cokes are fizzy cola drinks

explanation.surface: Someone sweet-talks by offering sodas to the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter someone is to cajole or wheedle them into doing something.

clue.text: Hurry, hide!

definitions.meaning: to hurry along quickly is to rush or dash
a hide is an animal skin with its fur

explanation.walkthrough: 'hide!' reads as an urgent order to conceal oneself, but it is a noun meaning skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing along at full speed and an animal skin with fur share one word.

clue.text: Greek character tense and strained

parts.note: tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A Greek person is nervous and under stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like a second definition but here it is the grammar abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope pulled tight is stretched or strained, with no slack in it.

clue.text: Make first monk that is welcoming sit back

parts.note: a prior is a monk in charge of a priory

indicators.note: welcoming means the that is letters take in the reversed sit between them

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: back means the word sit is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A monk is told to welcome guests while reclining.
explanation.definitionFit: To rank something as most urgent is to put it at the top of the list.

clue.text: Charge judge

definitions.meaning: a charge is a price or fee per unit
to judge is to assess or rank something

explanation.definitionFit: A price set per unit and the act of assessing quality share one word.

clue.text: Oppose token performance

parts.note: a counter is a token used in board games
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: Resistance to a show staged merely as a gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: To neutralise or work against something is to oppose its effect.
